To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the impact of IT-enabled learning mechanisms is dependent on a firm's internal/external learning strategies and the size of its partners and (b) a firm should select an appropriate knowledge management strategy based on the size of its own organization and that of its partners.

(1) IT-enabled mechanisms are effective in enhancing knowledge exploration and exploitation in interorganizational settings; (2) the size of a firm's partners affects the effectiveness of IT-enabled mechanisms in enhancing knowledge exploration; (3) the size of firm partners affects the effectiveness IT-enabled mechanisms in knowledge exploitation; and (4) a firm's learning strategy affects the effectiveness of knowledge exploration and knowledge exploitation.

the size of a firm's partners is an important factor in determining the optimal knowledge management strategies for the focal firm, that the size of the focal firm is an important factor determining the optimal knowledge exploration and exploitation strategies, and that fast learning from partners is particularly beneficial when a firm has a slow learning mechanism internally.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of IT and learning mechanisms in the interorganizational setting.
the impact of IT on knowledge exploration and exploitation in interorganizational settings and the role of partner size on this relationship.
the impact of IT on interorganizational learning and the implications for firm's learning strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IT enabled learning mechanisms are more beneficial to a small firm in an inter-organizational setting.
the size of a firm relative to the size of its partner(s) is important in determining the appropriate knowledge management strategy for that firm.
the impact of the learning mechanism and strategy on a firm's long term knowledge outcomes depends on the size of its partners.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IT enabled learning mechanisms are more beneficial for firms when they are used in combination and when the firm's internal learning strategy is fast.
the size of a firm relative to its partners is an important determinant of its learning mechanism and its knowledge outcomes.
a firm should select its learning mechanisms and strategies based on its size, its learning capability, and the learning capability of its partners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the learning strategy that a firm employs in an interorganization setting is contingent on the size of its partners and the IT mechanisms that it employs to learn.
the size of a firm's partners is important in determining the firm's learning strategy and that the size of the firm is important in selecting appropriate knowledge management strategies.
the learning strategy adopted by a firm has a strong impact on its long-term knowledge outcomes.
